findings.evidence: Root cause verified before fixing: the recorded evidence_manifest_sha256 was the CANONICAL-JSON digest (sorted keys, compact separators, no trailing newline) — the system's own documented convention (make_audit_request.py docstring; identical in every prior cycle's binding including auditor-passed ones: a75e2f7f, c1e973ca, c1c6bac9 all rec==canonical, rec!=raw-byte) — while the committed manifest file was pretty-printed, so its raw-byte digest differed. Your requirement that the file-level reference identify the file BY ITS BYTES is the stronger and better convention, so the fix removes the ambiguity at the writer rather than re-documenting it: make_audit_request.py now writes evidence_manifest.json in canonical byte form, making raw-byte and canonical digests IDENTICAL — one hash convention, verified at a9c5f0f5c90afd9036f900bcd31a43b103225874 (raw==canonical bytes: True; recorded==raw-byte sha: True). The generator patch also fixes this for all future cycles. No barrier extracted; publish_claim un-retried since its DENY.
